Also paced the backfill (EMBED_PACE_MS, default 21s between origins) because one embed request per origin back-to-back trips the provider per-minute limit; pacing lives in the backfill, not the embed layer, so live chat is never throttled. Gate PASS. Verified live: production reindexed to 21 chunks all on voyage-3.5-lite, 0 stale, and the chatbot now answers background questions from the profile origin.

features.title: Parse the persona into one knowledge entry per claim, and sweep the old ones on every save
features.notes: savePersona already reindexed, but as ONE origin: the whole paragraph competed for a retrieval slot on the average of everything it said, and the graph had a single edge owner called "Persona". lib/personaFacts.ts now splits the paragraph with one Claude call into {topic,text} claims (prompted to be self-contained, since each is retrieved without the surrounding paragraph), and indexPersona writes one origin per claim as fact:<slug> labeled "Persona — <topic>" — so each gets its own chunk, embedding, entity extraction and edge ownership. MAX_FACTS=8 is a spend limit: every entry costs an embedding request and an entity-extraction call on EVERY save, plus 21s of pacing in a full reindex. Failure is always a downgrade, never an error: no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, malformed JSON, a provider failure, or prose under MIN_SPLIT_CHARS(200) all index the paragraph whole under the single `persona` origin exactly as before. sweepPersonaOrigins drops every persona origin a pass did not write — required, because indexOrigin only replaces the id it is handed and retrieve() scans the whole chunk table with no origin filter, so a claim removed from the paragraph would otherwise keep being fed to the model as fact; it lives in indexPersona so reindex.ts and indexEverything sweep too, and it also retires the pre-feature single `persona` origin on the first save. The always-on PERSONA block is untouched — the full paragraph still ships verbatim every message. Proof: docs/features/persona-knowledge-entries/proof.ts (45 assertions green, fully offline — both model calls injected and an assertion pins embedModel to local-hash-256-v1 so it fails loudly if it ever goes online). persona-sections and universal-knowledge-index proofs still green; the latter's stub now passes split:async()=>[] so an unrelated proof does not make a Claude call. tsc + next lint clean.
features.next: Persona chunks now get more independent shots at a retrieval seed slot and eat more of the 6000-char budget, duplicating text the model already has in the always-on block. Excluding originKind=='persona' from retrieve() would fix it but breaks universal-knowledge-index/proof.ts:148 — decide deliberately. Also stale: universal-knowledge-index/FEATURE.md:24 and the prisma/schema.prisma:52-54 comment still call persona a singleton origin id. features.title: Deleting content removes its claims from the entity graph
features.notes: Deleting a source/project/photo/approved answer removed its Chunk + EntityMention rows but left every Entity and EntityEdge behind, with no provenance to clean them up. That was a live correctness bug, not just debris: retrieve() seeds entities by matching the raw query against ALL entity keys and renders their edges into the prompt as KNOWN RELATIONSHIPS, so a deleted source's extracted relations kept being stated as fact with no chunk supporting them. New EntityEdgeOrigin table records which origin asserted each edge; persistGraph claims edges for the indexing origin; dropOrigin retracts that origin's ownership, deletes edges left with no owner, and prunes entities with no mentions AND no edges. Cross-origin dedup is preserved — a relation two origins assert survives losing one. Edges with NO ownership rows are never auto-pruned, which protects hand-added Graph tab relations and every edge written before this table existed, so shipping it cannot empty an existing graph. clearOrigin was split into clearOriginChunks so a flaky extraction no longer retracts claims mid-reindex; an origin whose text becomes empty now retracts like a delete; mergeInto carries ownership onto rewired edges; deleteSource routes through dropOrigin instead of relying on the Source->Chunk cascade alone. Proof: docs/features/graph-delete-provenance/proof.ts (22 assertions green, was red on 3; the merge assertion verified independently red with lib/retrieval/graph.ts reverted). Gate PASS on this change; a later gate run fails inside the concurrent ai-drafted-answers work (lib/answerDrafts.ts), unrelated to this feature. Schema applied locally with prisma db push.
features.next: Deploy — `prisma db push` runs on start, so EntityEdgeOrigin is created automatically on Railway. Existing prod edges carry no ownership until `npx tsx scripts/reindex.ts --all` re-asserts it; until then they are treated as untracked and are never auto-pruned, so deletes won't retract pre-existing relations. Graph tab not clicked through (admin login required).

features.title: Expose the agent to other agents over A2A, plus a hosted agent facts card
features.notes: The site is now callable by other AI agents, not just readable by people. Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json (A2A v1.0 — the CURRENT spec; note v1.0 renamed nearly everything from the v0.3 shape most tutorials still show: supportedInterfaces replaces url/preferredTransport, PascalCase SendMessage replaces message/send, TASK_STATE_* replaces lowercase states, and the `kind` discriminator is gone). Both live generations are served: v1.0 and v0.3, negotiated by the A2A-Version header, with absent = 0.3 per §3.6.2, and the 0.3 card also at the legacy /.well-known/agent.json. Endpoints: /api/a2a (JSON-RPC + SSE) and /api/a2a/rest (HTTP+JSON), both thin wrappers over one dispatch() so the two bindings cannot drift. Methods: SendMessage, SendStreamingMessage, GetTask, ListTasks, CancelTask, SubscribeToTask; push-notification methods and the extended card return the specific -32003/-32004 the card's capabilities imply. NO SECOND BRAIN — lib/a2a/run.ts translates lib/brain.ts's {text,card} events into A2A messages/artifacts, and A2UI blocks become `data` parts, so a calling agent gets machine-readable projects instead of prose. New A2ATask table persists tasks in Postgres (an in-memory store would break GetTask across a redeploy) and contextId doubles as the chat sessionId, so agent traffic lands in Activity. Open by default but rate limited (A2A_RATE_LIMIT, default 30/min/IP); A2A_API_KEY closes it and the card then advertises the bearer scheme. Also /.well-known/agent-facts.json in NANDA AgentFacts format — self-hosted, with no fabricated audit claims (no evaluations block, certification.level = self-declared) — and a human /agent page linked from the homepage. Card and facts are both generated from the Profile row, so any site built from this template describes its own owner. Proof: docs/features/a2a-agent-interface/proof.ts (61 assertions green, zero Anthropic calls — it drives the real dispatcher over a seeded canned answer; verified red by breaking the 0.3 `final` flag and the card data-part). tsc + eslint clean. Verified live on the dev server: all three well-known docs 200, a real knowledge-base answer through /api/a2a, SSE streaming with card data parts, the REST binding on every path, non-blocking send + SubscribeToTask reattachment, and the /agent page in the browser.
features.next: Deploy — `prisma db push` runs on start, so A2ATask is created automatically on Railway. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL on Railway or the card will advertise the wrong host. Not done: gRPC binding, Agent Card JWS signing (needs a key story), and the two stale agentcards.host39.org cards under blakemauri2@gmail.com, which are near-empty and point at a dead URL — decide whether to repoint them at /.well-known/agent-card.json or delete them.

features.title: In-chat booking card backed by the real Google Calendar
features.notes: A second conversion path alongside the contact form: show_booking renders real open times pulled from Google free/busy, and picking one writes a confirmed event with a Meet link and emails the visitor an invite. Auth is an OAuth REFRESH TOKEN, not a service account — the calendar is a personal @gmail.com, where a robot identity can only be granted access by an explicit share and still couldn't invite as Blake. Scopes are deliberately calendar.freebusy + calendar.events only: the site sees WHEN he's busy and can add events, but cannot read meeting titles, guests or contents. No googleapis dependency (three fetch calls in lib/google.ts, following lib/github.ts). lib/booking/slots.ts is pure slot math — Intl-derived tz conversion with a second correction pass so DST is right, calendar-date day walking rather than +24h, buffers, lead time, horizon. EVERYTHING FAILS CLOSED: booking off, creds missing, token rejected, freeBusy returning a per-calendar `errors` entry inside a 200, network down — each yields zero slots, never the unsubtracted grid. The server never trusts a submitted start; createBooking recomputes open slots and refuses anything off the list. Booking.startsAt is UNIQUE and the row is claimed BEFORE the Google call, so a race has one winner and a failed insert releases the claim. Read path caches free/busy 60s; the write path always calls Google, because the unique constraint guards only this site's own bookings and a cached read there is a double-booking. Tool + prompt instructions are withheld from the model unless bookingEnabled AND Google is connected. Admin 'Booking' tab: connection status, availability settings, and the upcoming list. One-time authorization via `node scripts/google-auth.mjs`. Proof: docs/features/booking-card/proof.ts (39 assertions green, zero Google and zero Anthropic calls; verified red four ways — swallowing the freeBusy error, trusting the submitted slot, and serving the write path from cache, which booked a slot that had just been taken). Gate PASS; tsc + eslint clean (only the pre-existing Chat.tsx img warning). Card UI clicked through end to end in the browser: day/time picker, correct grouping across a UTC-day boundary into the VISITOR's timezone, details form, confirmation with Meet link.
features.next: NOT YET CONNECTED — the card stays hidden until Blake does the Google setup: create a Cloud project, enable the Calendar API, PUBLISH the consent screen (while it's in Testing, Google expires refresh tokens after 7 days and the card silently goes quiet), create a Web OAuth client with redirect http://localhost:5858/callback, then run `node scripts/google-auth.mjs` and set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/REFRESH_TOKEN in .env and on Railway. Then switch it on and set weekly hours on the admin Booking tab (the form pre-fills weekdays 9-5). `prisma db push` runs on start so the Booking table is created automatically on Railway. Not verified against a real Google account by Claude — that needs Blake's credentials. Admin tab not clicked through (login required). Out of scope and still unbuilt: cancel/reschedule from the site (Google's own invite handles it), multiple durations or calendars, per-date holiday overrides. Note the A2A channel receives a bare {type:'booking'} data part with no slots in it, which is not actionable for a calling agent — worth revisiting if agent-initiated booking is ever wanted.

features.title: Connect Google Calendar from the admin Booking tab (browser OAuth, encrypted token)
features.notes: Turning booking on used to mean a five-step terminal errand ending in a production env var. It is now a button. app/api/admin/google/{connect,callback} runs the consent flow (CSRF state in an httpOnly cookie, admin-gated, refusal logic pure in lib/googleConnection.decideCallback so the proof drives every gate); the refresh token is stored on Profile.googleRefreshToken encrypted with AES-256-GCM keyed from AUTH_SECRET, so a DB dump is not calendar write access. GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN in the environment still wins, so existing deploys are untouched, and scripts/google-auth.mjs stays as the escape hatch. Disconnect clears the row and revokes at Google. features.title: A2UI timeline card for work experience (show_timeline)
features.notes: Sixth A2UI card. "What is your background?" was the one question a personal site exists to answer with no card behind it — the model reassembled it from retrieved chunks, and dates and company names are exactly what a language model paraphrases away. show_timeline renders Profile.experience verbatim as a vertical timeline (rail + a dot per role, dates/role/company/description), headed by Profile.experienceSummary, Blake’s own paragraph. No schema change, no migration, no dependency: the data has been on the Profile row since the Experience editor shipped and only reached the chat as retrieval text. STORED ORDER IS PRESERVED, NOTHING IS SORTED — `dates` is free text ("2021–2024", "Summer ’19", "2023 – present"), and a parser that misreads one format silently reorders a correct history into a false one; chronology is a claim about Blake’s life and the code should not guess at it. Folds past 4 roles so a long career cannot push the conversation off the screen. Not withheld when empty, unlike show_booking: an empty booking card is a broken promise, an empty timeline is just an empty state, and a conditional tool would cost a Profile read on every message. Touched the standard six places (lib/cards.ts, app/cards/Cards.tsx, lib/brain.ts, lib/canned.ts, lib/knowledge.ts, README). Proof: docs/features/experience-timeline-card/proof.ts (30 assertions green, zero Anthropic calls and zero network — the hosted embedders are unset so buildSystemPrompt uses the local hashed one; verified red by stashing the five source files: "experienceTimelineBlock is not a function"). tsc + next lint were clean on this change. Server-rendered against the live theme and screenshotted in headless Chrome, which caught a bug all 27 functional assertions missed: the dot was var(--primary), and lib/theme.ts lets `surface` double as --primary, so the default palette painted a navy dot on a navy card and the timeline read as an indented list. Now --accent-on-bg-soft (derived by readableOn against that exact surface). No assertion guards it — contrast is not observable from textContent.
features.next: Visual regression of the dot/rail contrast is unguarded (see PROOF.md) — this repo has no screenshot-diff harness. Not clicked through inside a real chat bubble at real widths. Whether Haiku actually reaches for show_timeline on "what’s your background?" is a live model call the proof deliberately does not make. QUICK WIN: the first starter chip is already "What's your background and past experience?" — attaching show_timeline to that canned row on the Answers tab makes the card render instantly for free. The Experience editor has no reordering control, so the card’s order is append order plus whatever the resume parser produced; worth drag-to-reorder now that the order is visible to visitors. A2A emits the block as a plain data part, unexercised.

features.title: Suggested merges on the Graph tab (auto-detected duplicate entities, one-click merge)
features.notes: lib/retrieval/graph.ts suggestedMerges(): duplicate-entity pairs from two deterministic signals — condensed-key containment ('brambleworks' ⊂ 'brambleworksltd', shorter side ≥ 4 chars) and shared-neighbor overlap (Jaccard ≥ 0.5, ≥ 2 shared, both ≥ 2 neighbors) which ALSO requires a shared 3+-char name word, because nearly everything in this graph neighbors Blake and raw overlap would pair unrelated skills ('TypeScript'/'React') for a one-click merge. Survivor = more mentions, then more edges, then longer name. Capped at 20, containment ranked first, each unordered pair once. mergeEntities(from,into) is the one-click path through the existing mergeInto machinery, fail-soft on stale ids. UI: Suggested merges block atop the Entities pane (hidden when empty) + ⚠ count on the pane tab (no colour override — the tab background swaps with the theme); mergeSuggestedEntities server action is the standard thin auth+revalidate wrapper. No LLM call, no schema change. Proof: docs/features/graph-suggested-merges/proof.ts (18 assertions green, was red at 'suggestedMerges is not a function'; zero Anthropic calls). tsc + next lint clean on touched files. Evaluator PASS. Gate: initially failed in the concurrent session's mid-edit google-connect proof; after they fixed it, GATE: PASS with this feature's changes included.

features.title: Retrieval playground on the Graph tab: type a question, see what retrieve() returns
features.notes: Test retrieval box on the Graph tab: lib/retrieval/graph.ts retrievalPreview(query) returns the REAL retrieve() result shaped for display — chunks with origin ref, blended score, and rank/graph provenance, the KNOWN RELATIONSHIPS lines, plus queryEntities (the exact q.includes(key) match retrieve() uses to seed expansion, so the admin can see whether the graph even recognizes the question) and an indexEmpty flag for an honest empty state. previewRetrieval server action is auth-only (read-only, no revalidate); app/admin/RetrievalPlayground.tsx is a small client component (useTransition) above GraphView. Proof: docs/features/retrieval-playground/proof.ts (12 assertions green, was red at 'retrievalPreview is not a function'; zero Anthropic calls). PROOF LESSONS BAKED IN: (1) the draft asserted nonsense queries return zero chunks — false, retrieve() max-normalizes the vector signal so a non-empty index always scores something; replaced with a stronger byte-equivalence assertion (preview === retrieve() output, proving no second retrieval path). (2) Deleting VOYAGE/OPENAI keys before imports does NOT pin the local embedder — Prisma re-loads .env on import; delete AFTER imports. (3) To prove a graph-only hit, every seed slot must be filled by marker-bearing chunks AND the graph-hop chunk must be small enough to fit retrieve()'s 6000-char budget after ~5 seeds. tsc + lint clean; GATE: PASS; evaluator PASS.
features.next: indexEmpty:true branch unasserted (needs an empty DB); box not typed into in a browser (admin login required).
